name: Pisac ruins on foot
why: Climb from the market square of Pisac up the curved Inca terraces to the Intihuatana temple on the ridge, with the Sacred Valley under your feet.
book: Boleto Turístico del Cusco, cash in soles with your passport: sold at the control point at the town exit and at the upper entrance. The park is open 07:00-18:00. A lazier way: taxi to the upper entrance (about S/30-35) and walk down only.
water: No water is sold inside the park: carry 1.5 litres.
dangers: Steep stone steps and narrow ledges with drops beside the terraces.
Loose gravel on parts of the path; slippery in the rainy season.
Strong sun at 3,000-3,400 m: hat and sunscreen.
turnaround: Be out of the ruins before dark: the site is isolated and closes at 18:00.

points.name: Pisac market square
points.note: The plaza and Sunday market by the church of San Pedro. The path starts to its left and climbs along the Kitamayo stream.

points.name: Pisac terraces
points.note: Past the fork above the fields the right branch crosses the stream and climbs straight up the Inca terraces to the watchtowers on the ridge.

points.name: Intihuatana of Pisac
points.note: The ceremonial sector: the sun stone and fine Inca temples on the ridge, about 3,350 m. Walk down the same way, keeping the mountain on your right.
